overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation. A two-councilor discussion is below quorum and not deliberation, and the serial-deliberation and off-the-record negotiation theories lacked factual support.

allegations.summary: Two councilors allegedly discussed an amendment to a policy order between the June 2 and June 9 meetings, outside any noticed meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Regardless, the discussion that forms the basis of the complaint was between two councilors, which is less than a quorum of the Council and therefore did not constitute deliberation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged serial deliberation because one councilor sponsored the policy order and the other did not; AG found only speculation.
allegations.key_passage: we have consistently explained that mere speculation or conjecture regarding deliberation outside of a posted meeting, without factual support, is insufficient to support a complaint’s allegations.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the amendment was negotiated off the record by two councilors, which the Open Meeting Law prohibits.
allegations.key_passage: Instead, the video recording of the June 9 meeting shows that Councilor McGovern and Councilor Siddiqui had some discussion regarding opening the Westley Avenue entrance to Linear Park during which Councilor Siddiqui mentioned timed gates.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
